description: Build the match orchestrator (src/lib/range-runtime/) that is the ONLY code in the repo allowed to talk to Docker: it builds a hardened image from /range-target/ (from FEAT-001), runs one ephemeral container per match on an internal-only per-match network, enforces resource/time limits, captures logs into audit_logs, exposes an admin kill switch, and proves isolation with a self-test. Depends on FEAT-001 existing (the image it builds and the health/vault endpoints it probes come from the target app just built).
steps: Create src/lib/range-runtime/dockerClient.ts: a thin wrapper around Node's built-in http/https request functions that parses DOCKER_HOST (unix:///path or tcp://host:port, falling back to /run/user/1000/podman/podman.sock style default or the OS default docker socket) once at module load and exposes typed helpers (createNetwork, removeNetwork, createContainer, startContainer, stopContainer, removeContainer, inspectContainer, getContainerStats, getContainerLogs, execInContainer) that each issue one HTTP call to the Engine API — no dockerode dependency.

Create /range-target/Dockerfile (FROM node:22-alpine, the already-pulled base image) that COPYs the app source into the image (no bind mount), installs only production deps, runs as a non-root user, and ships a small entrypoint script that, on container start, copies /app's source into a tmpfs working directory and execs node from there (so later a patch write to the tmpfs + restart is possible without any host mount) — implements the 'live patching via tmpfs' decision.

Create src/lib/range-runtime/orchestrator.ts exposing startMatch(matchId) / stopMatch(matchId) that: creates a per-match Docker network with internal:true and no published ports, starts one container attached to it with --read-only, a small tmpfs for /app and /tmp, --cap-drop ALL, --security-opt no-new-privileges, default seccomp, non-root user, memory/cpu/pids limits (0.5 CPU, 256MB, pid limit), and a hard timeout (e.g. 25 min) enforced by a setTimeout in the orchestrator that force-destroys the container+network if still running; records container id, network id, started_at into a new range_target_matches table (via src/lib/db.ts additions, see next step).

Extend src/lib/db.ts initSchema() with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS range_target_matches (id, match_session_id, container_id, network_id, status, vault_balance_cents, started_at, ended_at, timeout_at) and add helper functions getRangeMatch/updateRangeMatch/endRangeMatch following the same style as endMatch/endStaleMatches; all state transitions go through recordAuditLog with actions like RANGE_MATCH_STARTED/RANGE_MATCH_TIMEOUT/RANGE_MATCH_KILLED.

Pipe the running container's stdout/stderr (via the Engine API's container logs/attach endpoint) and the target app's own access log (expose it via a small /__logs endpoint added in range-target, or tail the container's log stream) into recordAuditLog entries tagged with the match id, on an interval or streamed — this satisfies 'all container stdout/stderr and the target's access log captured into audit_logs'.

Create the admin kill switch: new src/app/api/range/admin/kill/route.ts (POST) that checks getCurrentUser() + is_operator (same inline pattern as src/app/api/admin/route.ts), accepts a matchId, and calls orchestrator.stopMatch(matchId) immediately, recording a RANGE_MATCH_KILLED audit log entry including the operator's user id.

Write an isolation self-test: tests/range-target/isolation.test.ts (part of the range-target test job, not main npm test) that starts a real match container via the orchestrator and proves, from inside the match's own network context (e.g. by running a short-lived probe container or exec'ing a curl/wget check inside the target container itself, since the container has no egress) that it CANNOT reach the host, the internet (e.g. a known public IP/DNS lookup fails or times out), or a second match's container/network — then force-destroys everything it created.
acceptance_criteria: orchestrator.startMatch() produces a running container reachable only via its internal Docker network (no published ports) and orchestrator.stopMatch() reliably destroys both the container and its network

resource limits are applied; memory/cpu/pids settings that have no measurable effect under rootless Podman are logged as a warning (per ASSUMPTIONS.md) rather than silently assumed to work or causing a crash
a match left running past the configured timeout is force-destroyed automatically
tests/range-target/isolation.test.ts passes: no route to host, internet, or a second match's container
the kill switch route force-destroys a running match's container+network immediately and is rejected with 403 for a non-operator user
range_target_matches rows and audit_logs entries exist for a full start->stop cycle, auditable after the fact
verification: PATH=.tools/node22/bin:$PATH npm run test:range-target — isolation self-test and any orchestrator unit tests pass

manually: PATH=.tools/node22/bin:$PATH node -e "require('tsx/cjs'); ..." or a small script invoking startMatch()/stopMatch() once, confirm via `docker ps`/`docker network ls` the container and network appear then disappear, and confirm no container/network created during this verification is left behind afterward (`docker ps -a`, `docker network ls` show none of this task's resources)
PATH=.tools/node22/bin:$PATH npm test — still fully passing (new range_target_matches schema addition must not break existing matchLifecycle/backendSource tests)
PATH=.tools/node22/bin:$PATH npm run build — still passes, run only when no `npm run dev` is active
git commit this section's changes as one commit
findings: Orchestrator in src/lib/range-runtime/{dockerClient,orchestrator}.ts (only Docker access). API: startMatch(matchId,{userId?,timeoutMs?}) -> RangeMatchRow (builds image cynchor-range-target:1 once per process via POST /build of range-target/ tar, creates internal network range-net-<id>, container range-target-<id>, waits for /healthz via exec, verifies cgroup limits); stopMatch(matchId,{userId?,reason?:'ENDED'|'TIMEOUT'|'KILLED',details?}) -> boolean (idempotent, flushes logs first). Both keyed by match_session_id (any string). Exports RANGE_LABEL='cynchor.range' (every container/network carries it; also cynchor.range.match=<rtm id>), LIMITS, DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS=25min, listByLabel. dockerClient also exposes execInContainer(id,cmd)->{exitCode,output}, inspectContainer, inspectNetwork, getContainerStats, getContainerLogs. DB (src/lib/db.ts): table range_target_matches + createRangeMatch/getRangeMatch/getRangeMatchById/getActiveRangeMatch/updateRangeMatch/endRangeMatch; statuses STARTING/RUNNING/ENDED/TIMEOUT/KILLED/FAILED. updateRangeMatch uses a fixed COALESCE statement because tests/rangeTargetSqlIsolation.test.ts forbids interpolated SQL in src/. Audit actions: RANGE_MATCH_STARTED/ENDED/TIMEOUT/KILLED/FAILED, RANGE_CONTAINER_LOG (stdout/stderr incl. target 'ACCESS METHOD path status' lines, polled every 5s + final flush), RANGE_LIMIT_WARNING. Kill route POST /api/range/admin/kill {matchId}: 403 non-operator, 404 none running. Target changes: range-target/Dockerfile, entrypoint.sh (cp -R /opt/target -> tmpfs /app, restart loop; a live patch = write into /app then kill node, the loop restarts it), server.js now logs ACCESS lines to stdout. Do NOT set NODE_ENV=production in the image (disables seeding). Rootless Podman facts: tmpfs option uid= is rejected (use mode=1777); Podman inspect HostConfig.CapDrop shows an expanded list not ['ALL'], so verify caps via /proc/self/status CapEff==0 (it is) and NoNewPrivs=1; memory/pids/cpu limits ARE effective (cgroup memory.max=268435456, pids.max=128, cpu.max=50000 100000), so no RANGE_LIMIT_WARNING fired. Internal network: container cannot reach second match, host (gateway, host IPs, 10.0.2.2), 1.1.1.1 or DNS; positive control passes. Containers have no host-reachable port, so FEAT-003's proxy/scorer cannot HTTP in from the host: use execInContainer (wget -q -O - http://127.0.0.1:8080/...) or add a way to reach the internal network (not done here). Orchestrator timers are in-process only: no reaper on server restart (orphans carry the cynchor.range label; listByLabel can clean them). Tests use CYNCHOR_DB_PATH=.test.sqlite.range (gitignored by .test.sqlite*). Ran: npm run test:range-target -> 12/12 pass (7 exploit + 5 isolation incl. timeout and kill); manual startMatch/stopMatch script showed container+network appear then vanish; npm test -> 39/39; npm run build -> compiled OK (no dev server running). docker ps -a / network ls show only pre-existing buildx_buildkit_default and bridge afterwards; nothing left to clean.
